Scientific name: Trichomycterus auroguttatus Costa, 1992.

Size: 61 mm SL.

Type locality: Rio Marimbondo, tributary of Rio Preto, Rio Paraiba basin, 1 kilometer west of Visconde de Mauá, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

Etymology: Trichomycterus comes from the Greek trichos, meaning hair, and mykter, meaning nose; in reference to the barbels.

IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated.
South America: Marimbondo River, tributary of the Preto River, Paraíba do Sul River basin. Rio de Janeiro State.
This genus takes live or frozen food, as well as commercial dry prepared foods. Be careful not to overfeed. In nature, they feed on small invertebrates living at the bottom.
Revue française d'Aquariologie Herpétologie v. 18 (no. 4) [for 1991], pp 105, Fig. 6.
